This project is a Wokwi design created for the Tiny Tapeout Workshop in Malaga, implementing a 4-bit linear-feedback shift register with reset. All documentation sections contain placeholder text, so the feedback taps and reset polarity are not documented. A 10 MHz clock is specified, but no pins or external hardware are listed. The only concrete information is the 4-bit LFSR with reset intent.

This is an 8-bit MIPS-inspired single-cycle processor with eight registers, an ALU, branches and jumps, scaled to fit one Tiny Tapeout tile. It runs a hardcoded program automatically after reset; three input pins select which register is shown on the eight outputs, while five bidirectional pins expose the program counter and one shows a halt flag. Testing needs only LEDs on the outputs and switches on the register-select inputs, with no external hardware required. It is notable for preserving core MIPS concepts in a very small area, though the documentation does not report silicon results.

All documentation sections contain placeholder text, so the method of displaying the numbers (such as LEDs or a seven-segment display) is unknown. No pins, clock frequency, or external hardware are specified. The design is essentially undocumented beyond its title and one-line description.
